balance.argument_a: The Worst-Case Stack is the conservative, defensible-to-a-safety-reviewer choice: it guarantees release under every combination of in-spec parts, with no dependence on a statistical-independence assumption that a single flight joint (as opposed to a large production run) cannot really be checked against. At today's real n=3 build it clears both of NASA-adjacent industry's thresholds with real room to spare -- margin 4.17 against the 1.25 gapping floor and 2.00 release-element floor (Appendix B) -- using only a direct sum of Appendix C's 3 real per-supplier tolerances (0.0079in + 0.0050in + 0.0039in = 0.0168in total), with no correction factor, no independence assumption, and no statistical model to defend if a reviewer pushes back on any single number.
balance.argument_b: The Modified RSS Stack is the real, industry-standard method for production tolerance stacking -- not naive textbook RSS, but RSS corrected by the well-documented x1.5 Bender/Motorola factor that real practitioners apply precisely because printed supplier tolerances don't reliably behave like true 3-sigma bounds. It still predicts a materially tighter band than Worst-Case, passing more of the individually in-spec parts already in hand without requesting rework or replacement from suppliers who did nothing wrong -- while already carrying a real-world conservatism correction that pure RSS lacks.
balance.margin_basis: Compare the Worst-Case Stack's and Modified RSS Stack's predicted total tolerance against the real, cited gapping-margin (1.25) and release-element-margin (>2.00) thresholds (Appendix B -- sourced to a 2012 SNC/ESMATS engineering paper, S2, not to GD-ED-2214 itself, which states only a qualitative no-gapping criterion), both at the current n=3 build (D4) and as a limiting trend as n grows (D1-D3), using Appendix E MA4's disclosed 0.070in nominal gapping-allowance bridge to convert the dimensionless margin factors into a comparison against Appendix C/D's dimensional tolerance-stack values.
balance.margin_pct_definition: Percent difference between the Worst-Case Stack's and Modified RSS Stack's predicted total tolerance at n=3 (today's build): (0.0168 - 0.01520) / 0.0168 = 9.55% ~ 9.6%. RETUNE (2026-08-30): the original model used naive, uncorrected RSS (0.0101in at n=3), giving a 39.9% margin that failed this project's <=20% balance ceiling. Research found real tolerance-stacking practice does not use naive RSS -- it uses RSS x1.5 (Appendix F, S6), a real, well-documented correction Bender introduced in 1962 and Motorola later standardized, specifically because RSS's own independence/3-sigma assumptions (the same assumptions Argument A already distrusts) are known to be optimistic. Modeling Option B as this real, corrected version of RSS -- not a different n, not an invented allowance -- brings the two methods to 9.6% apart at n=3. At n=3 BOTH methods still clear both of Appendix B's thresholds under the MA4 margin model (WC margin 4.17, Modified RSS margin 4.61) -- this remains the live dilemma, not a foregone conclusion. The methods still diverge as n grows, exactly as before: the Worst-Case Stack's margin against the release-element threshold (>=2.00) falls from 2.08 at n=6 to 1.79 at n=7 (FAILS), and by n=10 sits exactly at the 1.25 gapping-margin floor (1.250) while still failing the release-element margin. The Modified RSS Stack clears both thresholds at every modeled n (3, 6, 7, 10), with margins 4.61, 3.40, 3.15, 2.64 respectively.
balance.winning_option: B (the Modified RSS Stack) -- but only once the case's scaling frame (D1-D3) is engaged. At n=3 alone neither option is disqualified by Appendix B's thresholds, and the two methods' predicted tolerances are now genuinely close (9.6% apart); the case is built so that a Hero who stops at n=3 sees a real, close call, not an obvious winner. Under the growing-supplier-count frame the case forces (Anchor 3 / the Twist), Option B is the more durable choice: it is the only one of the two that continues to clear both of NASA-adjacent industry's real design-margin thresholds across the full modeled range (n=3 through n=10), while Option A (Worst-Case) fails the release-element margin starting at n=7 and sits at the edge of failing the gapping margin too by n=10. This is a genuine consequence of Worst-Case growing linearly in n while Modified RSS grows like 1.5*sqrt(n) (Appendix D) -- a constant multiplier does not change which growth rate wins -- not an artifact of the specific 0.070in allowance chosen in MA4 or of the x1.5 correction factor: a different allowance moves WHERE the crossover happens, not WHETHER Worst-Case eventually falls behind Modified RSS.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Future supplier-interface counts used to extend Appendix D beyond this build's real 3-supplier joint
modeling_assumptions.basis: n=6 is the last count at which the Worst-Case Stack clears NASA-adjacent industry's release-element margin threshold under MA4's model; n=7 is the first count at which it fails; n=10 is where Worst-Case sits almost exactly at the gapping-margin floor.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Shifts where D1's table samples the trend; does not change which method grows faster (n vs. sqrt(n)) or the location of the crossover, both fixed by Appendix C's real tolerances and the two real formulas.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Rows beyond n=3 in Appendix D use one equal, average per-interface tolerance rather than each future supplier's own distinct value
modeling_assumptions.value: 0.0056 in (average of Appendix C's three real tolerances)
modeling_assumptions.basis: No real per-supplier tolerance values exist for interfaces that don't exist yet on a future joint design; using this build's own real, cited tolerances as the averaging basis keeps the extension grounded rather than invented.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Affects the exact numbers in later Appendix D rows but not the qualitative finding (ratio's horizontal asymptote at 0), which depends only on the n vs. sqrt(n) structure.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Nominal diameter of the clampband/flange interface and nominal height of the preload bolt+shim stack
modeling_assumptions.value: 15.000 in (381.0 mm) diameter; 0.500 in (12.7 mm) stack height
modeling_assumptions.basis: No real program's specific dimensions are named; chosen as representative of a small-satellite Marman-clampband separation system, and used to select which ISO 2768-1 dimension-range row governs each interface's real, cited tolerance.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Could shift which ISO 2768-1 range row applies, changing the specific tolerance values, but not the comparison between the Worst-Case and Modified RSS formulas themselves.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Nominal per-joint gapping allowance used to convert Appendix B's real, cited dimensionless load-safety-factor margins (1.25, 2.00) into a comparison against Appendix C/D's real, cited dimensional tolerance-stack values
modeling_assumptions.value: 0.070 in; margin = 0.070in / predicted total tolerance; pass if margin >= threshold
modeling_assumptions.basis: No public source publishes a formula connecting a dimensional tolerance-stack value to these load-based factors for a general clampband joint. This case states its own transparent, disclosed conversion rule rather than inventing a nonexistent 'real' formula.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: MOST LOAD-BEARING ASSUMPTION IN THE CASE. Chosen so the Worst-Case/release-element-margin crossover lands inside the modeled range (n=6-7). A different allowance moves WHERE the crossover happens, not WHETHER Worst-Case eventually falls behind Modified RSS (fixed by n vs. sqrt(n) growth; the x1.5 factor on RSS, MA-adjacent but sourced to S6 rather than invented, does not change this).

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA4's 0.070in nominal gapping allowance bridges Appendix B's dimensionless load-safety margins (1.25, 2.00) to Appendix C/D's dimensional tolerance-stack values. No public source -- not GD-ED-2214, not the Lazansky/SNC paper -- publishes a formula connecting the two for a general clampband joint; this is a genuinely irreducible unknown (no amount of further research finds a real, citable bridging figure), not a proprietary number being estimated from an analogue. Tier 2 Probe 5 (2026-08-31) confirmed this is also the single dial whose flex actually flips the case's real recommendation logic: -50% (0.035in) drives BOTH options below Appendix B's release-element threshold at n=10, collapsing the winner from B to a tie-by-disqualification. This matches, and mechanically confirms, what case.md/case.json/FACILITATOR.md already call this case's single most load-bearing assumption -- it is disclosed here, not eliminated, because no more defensible allowance value exists to substitute.

The x1.5 Bender/Motorola correction factor (Appendix F, S6) is real, HIGH-confidence, directly-quoted cited data, not an author-invented modeling assumption -- it is included here anyway because Tier 2 Probe 5's explicit stress-test (2026-08-31, run via --flex-all, outside P5's doctrinal FLEX[] scope) found it is the one cited dial whose flex genuinely wobbles the case's real recommendation. -50% (factor -> 0.75) only strengthens Option B (worst-case margin across the modeled n range nearly doubles, to 5.27). +50% (factor -> 2.25) is NOT survived: Modified RSS's own predicted tolerance at n=10 then exceeds NASA-adjacent industry's release-element threshold, disqualifying B too and collapsing the winner to a tie-by-disqualification -- the same failure mode MA4's flex produces, from the opposite dial. This is disclosed, not eliminated, because S6 is the real, sourced, industry-standard value (verified live and unchanged against the primary Scholz/Boeing report, 2026-08-31 P6 data-decay pass) -- there is no more-defensible correction factor to substitute; a facilitator should use this asymmetry live in discussion (see FACILITATOR.md's Twist) rather than treat the case's 'B wins durably' finding as unconditionally stable.

sensitivity_note: NONE (SPEC §6). This is a mechanical-engineering quality/tolerancing trade-off with no protected-subject flag — consistent with the concept sheet's own assessment.

cohort_bands.note: The 45-minute Socratic plan (FACILITATOR.md) runs as written, with two deep-conflict threads at 20:00-30:00 (safety-conservatism vs. cost/rework-efficiency; single-build adequacy vs. long-run scalability of the sign-off policy).

Anchors 2 and 3 combine into a single pass. The twist still drops at 15:00, but only one deep-conflict thread runs (safety-conservatism vs. cost/rework-efficiency); the scalability thread folds into the close-out discussion. Total runtime shortens proportionally.

There is no vote to take. Anchor 1 becomes a stated initial position instead of a cold-call vote. The guide plays devil's advocate directly, arguing the other stack-up method's case. The twist still lands, but 'who reverses' becomes 'would you reverse, and why.'
